subtitle: Ask whether the net can, must or never reach a marking
placeholder: Type a CTL formula in English...
grammar.ag: A — for all paths. Combine with a temporal operator: always = AG, eventually = AF, next = AX
grammar.ef: E — some path exists. Combine with a temporal operator: always = EG, eventually = EF, next = EX
grammar.g: G — globally: AG with "for all paths", EG with "exists path"
grammar.f: F — finally: AF with "for all paths", EF with "exists path"
grammar.x: X — next state: AX with "for all paths", EX with "exists path". At a deadlock, AX is true and EX is false
grammar.u: E[A U B] — some path where condition A holds at every step until condition B holds. Write it between the two conditions, with no AND: exists path (A) until (B)
idle: Write a formula or pick an example
noResult: The verdict appears here after you verify a formula.
standardEmpty: The equivalent CTL formula appears here once the query is valid.
pathHint: Tip: "exists path eventually …" also returns the shortest path that reaches the state.
grammar.enabled: enabled(t0, t1): at least one of the transitions is enabled
statesList: Show the {count} states where it holds
grammar.au: A[A U B] — on every path, A holds until B holds: for all paths (A) until (B)
grammar.deadlock: deadlock: no transition is enabled (dead marking). EX is false and AX is true there
grammar.quoted: `B`: quote a place name that clashes with a keyword (B, x, t, In...)
grammar.linear: p0 + p1 >= 2: linear sums with + - and constant factors (2*p0), and place-to-place comparisons (p0 <= p1). Write spaces around - since hyphens can be part of names; no place*place
